stories.title: Pakistan's trade gap with Gulf partners narrows
summary: ISLAMABAD: Pakistan’s trade deficit with Gulf partner countries narrowed 26.35 per cent to $2.85bn in the first quarter of 2026-27 against $3.87bn a year earlier, largely due to lower imports and moderately higher exports.
On the export side, the UAE accounted for approximately 66.21pc of Pakistan’s total exports to the seven countries in 1QFY27, followed by Saudi Arabia at 19.45pc.
Exports to Qatar fell by nearly 22.79pc, while imports dipped by 72.51pc in 1QFY27 year on year.

summary: GWADAR: Pakistan reopened its border crossing with Iran at Gabd-Rimdan on Saturday, restoring bilateral trade and allowing stranded trucks carrying LPG and essential food commodities to resume movement after a weeklong suspension that began on Oct 17.

stories.title: Snow leopards face growing threats in Gilgit-Baltistan: experts
summary: GILGIT: The snow leopard, an iconic yet increasingly threatened species, faces mounting risks to its survival in Gilgit-Baltistan, which hosts Pakistan’s largest snow leopard habitat.

Experts and environmentalists said the protection of snow leopards remained a low priority, with no proper population monitoring or scientific research conducted in Gilgit-Baltistan, which accounts for the largest share of Pakistan’s snow leopard habitat.
Gilgit-Baltistan Chief Conservator of Parks and Wildlife Zakir Hussain said the snow leopard population was declining in the region due to human-induced factors.

stories.title: Revenue target for NHA more than doubled, says minister
summary: LAHORE: Federal Minister for Communication Abdul Aleem Khan says that the revenue target for National Highway Authority (NHA) for the ongoing fiscal year has been increased from Rs66 billion to Rs160 billion and its expenditures have also been capped at Rs50 billion.
The minister said that the Lahore-Sialkot Motorway was planned to be widened from four to six lanes with the additional Rs10 billion from the NHA-generated revenues.

He urged the NHA to consult major chambers of commerce before increasing toll taxes, explaining that higher toll charges directly increase freight and transportation costs and ultimately affect business competitiveness.
